items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to qualifying health care
costs and case management services under the New York state medical indemnity
fund; and to amend chapter 517 of the laws of 2016, amending the public health
law relating to payments from the New York state medical indemnity fund, in
relation to the effectiveness thereof
items.lawCode: Amd §2999-h, add §2999-k, Pub Health L; amd §5, Chap 517 of 2016
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8591

SPONSOR: KRUEGER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to qualifying health
care costs and case management services under the New York state medical
indemnity fund; and to amend chapter 517 of the laws of 2016, amending
the public health law relating to payments from the New York state
medical indemnity fund, in relation to the effectiveness thereof

 
PURPOSE:

To add and amend certain definitions and provisions of Title 4 of the
Public Health Law, regarding the New York State Medical Indemnity Fund
(MIF), in order to institute a new enrollee orientation, provide clar-
ification of qualifying health care costs, improve reimbursement proce-
dures, and make permanent the reimbursement rate established in 2016.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends section 2999-h of the Public Health Law by adding
definitions of "activities of daily living," "custodial care," and
"instrumental activities of daily living," and amends the definition of
"qualifying health care costs."

Section 2: Amends section 2999-j of the Public Health Law by adding
subdivision 4-a. Stipulates that qualifying health care costs incurred
for services rendered and supplies utilized by qualified plaintiffs in
the home or in a residential or other facility are to be paid from the
MIF. Directs the Commissioner to promulgate regulations regarding bill-
ing procedures and reimbursement calculation methodology for qualifying
health care costs.

Section 3: Amends Title 4 of the Public Health Law by adding sections
2999-k, "Case management," and 2999-1, "Explanation of benefits forms
relating to claims for qualifying health care costs under the fund."

Section 4: Removes the sunset on reimbursement rates for certain health
care services that were enacted in 2016 and that are set to expire in
December 2022.

Section 5: Establishes the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The New York State Medical Indemnity Fund ("MIF") was a Medicaid Rede-
sign Team Initiative enacted in 2011, to provide a funding source for
future health care costs for infants who sustained birth-related neuro-
logical injuries, in order to reduce medical malpractice premium costs.
MIF Enrollees are plaintiffs in medical malpractice actions who have
received either court-approved settlements or judgments deeming the
plaintiffs' neurological impairments to be birth-related. Participation
in the MIF is mandatory.

In 2016, MIF statute was amended to address several issues related to
MIF administration and improve access to care, including increasing
reimbursement rates that were inadequate for certain health care
services and stipulating that the MIF should pay for qualifying health
care costs that have an ancillary benefit to other members of the house-
hold.

This legislation seeks to address additional issues with MIF adminis-
tration that have been identified by MIF participants and stakeholders,
including: clarification of qualifying health care costs; codification
of case management functions, including orientation for new enrollees;
promulgation of regulations for billing procedures and reimbursement
calculation methodology for qualifying health care costs incurred in the
home, or in a residential or other facility; clarification of health
care practitioners who can provide care and inform determinations of
medical necessity; and provision of clear and detailed explanation of
benefits forms to MIF participants for claims related to qualifying
health care costs.

In addition, the 2016 reimbursement rate adjustments for certain health
care services expires on December 31, 2022. This legislation will make
those rates permanent, allowing MIF participants to access the health
care providers they need.

Children who have sustained birth-related neurological injuries due to
malpractice should have necessary health care services paid for by the
MIF, particularly since they are required to participate in the fund.
The provisions of this bill will help to improve access to these impor-
tant health care services, as well as help MIF families understand how
the MIF works and utilize MIF benefits.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it shall have
become a law. Effective immediately, the addition, amendment and/or
repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the implementation of
this act on its effective date are authorized to be made and completed
on or before such effective date.

BILL NUMBER: S8591A    Revise 7/28/22

SPONSOR: KRUEGER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to qualifying health
care costs under the New York state medical indemnity fund; and to amend
chapter 517 of the laws of 2016, amending the public health law relating
to payments from the New York state medical indemnity fund, in relation
to the effectiveness thereof

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill would add and amend certain definitions and provisions of
Title 4 of the Public Health Law, regarding the New York State Medical
Indemnity Fund (MIF), in order to provide clarification of qualifying
health care costs, improve reimbursement procedures, and make permanent
the reimbursement rate established in 2016.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill amends section 2999-h of the Public Health Law by
adding definitions of "activities of daily living" and "instrumental
activities of daily living," and amends the definition of "qualifying
health care costs."

Section 2 amends Title 4 of the Public Health Law by adding section
2999-k, "Explanation of benefits forms relating to claims for qualifying
health care costs under the fund," to stipulate that the fund adminis-
trator shall provide qualified plaintiffs with an explanation of bene-
fits form with specific information.

Section 3 removes the sunset on reimbursement rates for certain health
care services that were enacted in 2016 and that are set to expire in
December 2022.

Section 4 establishes the effective date.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION:

This bill will provide clarification of qualifying health care costs,
improve reimbursement procedures, and make permanent the reimbursement
rate established in 2016.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The New York State Medical Indemnity Fund ("MIF") was a Medicaid Rede-
sign Team Initiative enacted in 2011, to provide a funding source for
future health care costs for infants who sustained birth-related neuro-
logical injuries, in order to reduce medical malpractice premium costs.
MIF Enrollees are plaintiffs in medical malpractice actions who have
received either court-approved settlements or judgments deeming the
plaintiffs' neurological impairments to be birth-related.  Participation
in the MIF is mandatory.

In 2016, MIF statute was amended to address several issues related to
MIF administration and improve access to care, including increasing
reimbursement rates that were inadequate for certain health care
services and stipulating that the MIF should pay for qualifying health
care costs that have an ancillary benefit to other members of the house-
hold.

This legislation seeks to address additional issues with MIF adminis-
tration that have been identified by MIF participants and stakeholders
surrounding qualifying health care costs and claims reimbursement. Bill
provisions provide clarification of qualifying health care costs, and
health care practitioners who can provide care and inform determinations
of medical necessity, as well as clarification that qualifying health
care costs are to be reimbursed for services and supplies provided in
the home, or in a residential or other facility. This bill aims to
improve claims reimbursement by stipulating certain information that
shall be included in explanation of benefits forms to MIF participants
for claims related to qualifying health care costs.

In addition, the 2016 reimbursement rate adjustments for certain health
care services expires on December 31, 2022. This legislation will make
those rates permanent, allowing MIF participants to access the health
care providers they need.

Children who have sustained birth-related neurological injuries due to
malpractice should have necessary health care services paid for by the
MIF, particularly since they are required to participate in the fund.
The provisions of this bill will help to improve access to these impor-
tant health care services, as well as help MIF families understand how
the MIF works and utilize MIF benefits.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately, provided however that sections
one and two of this act shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it
shall have become a law. Effective immediately, the addition, amendment
and/or repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the implementation
of this act on its effective date are authorized to be made and
completed on or before such effective date.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 90 Chapter 807
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 8591-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend the public health law, in relation to qualifying
        health care costs under the New  York  state  medical  indemnity
        fund; and to amend chapter 517 of the laws of 2016, amending the
        public  health  law relating to payments from the New York state
        medical indemnity fund, in relation to the effectiveness  there-
        of"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This  bill  expands  the costs of medical procedures reimbursed by the
Medical Indemnity Fund (the Fund). The Fund was established in  2011  to
provide  funding  to  cover all future health care costs of patients who
have birth-related neurological injuries resulting from medical malprac-
tice at the time  of  delivery.  Specifically,  this  legislation  would
expand  the definition of "qualifying health care cost" for patients and
establish definitions for "activities of daily living" and "instrumental
activities of daily living."
 
  Expansion of costs by the Fund will have significant financial ramifi-
cations on the solvency of the Fund and, therefore, must  be  considered
within  the  context of the State Budget, which I am committed to doing.
The existing enhanced reimbursement rates, which many individuals in the
Fund rely on to pay for health care  services,  are  set  to  expire  on
December  31,  2022.  Through  an  agreement  with the Legislature, I am
committing to extend these rates for the next three years.  Any  further
changes  must  be discussed in the context of the State's budget negoti-
ations.
 
  On the basis of this agreement, I am pleased to sign  this  bill  into
law.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL

                                ______
